## CLAIMED, AND THE CHOSEN FIX (satisfies the AC that the decision + rejected option be recorded)

**CHOSEN: option B — DC's `set_parent` writes the EPIC LINK through the Agile API for a non-sub-task
child.** The emit gate is left ALONE.

Why this one, in the terms the ACs ask for:

 * It makes the two gates OVERLAP without touching either policy. The emit gate already emits exactly
   when the local parent's `ticket_type` is `epic` (`outbound_field_diff._resolve_local_parent:136-139`).
   Teaching the DC apply side to accept an EPIC parent for a non-sub-task child is therefore all that is
   required for the sets to intersect — and it intersects on the SHAPE THE EMIT GATE ALREADY PREFERS.
 * **It satisfies "the 8b25 hierarchy guard's Cloud behaviour is UNCHANGED" for free**, because no line
   of the emit path changes. `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/conflict/test_parent_hierarchy_guard.py` keeps
   passing as-is, which is the strongest form of that AC — untouched code, not re-argued code.
 * It is what the transport's OWN docstring already prescribes as the lift: "epic-link field id +
   `add_issues_to_epic` against a real DC instance under `agile_rest_path='greenhopper'`"
   (`adapters/jira_datacenter/transport.py:675-689`). The decline at :695-710 was written as a
   placeholder for exactly this work, naming the mechanism. I am implementing the thing the author
   deferred, not inventing a route.

**REJECTED: option A — teach the emit gate DC's sub-task shape** (emit a parent when the child is a
sub-task, whose parent is a standard issue). Rejected for three reasons:
 1. it would require the emit gate to become DEPLOYMENT-AWARE, so a Cloud-correct hierarchy policy starts
    branching on backend — the exact coupling the Jira-family seam (ADR 0035 / J2) exists to prevent;
 2. rebar's local model has no `sub-task` type at all (types are epic/story/task/bug), so "the child is a
    sub-task" is not expressible locally without inventing a fifth type or leaking a remote concept
    inward;
 3. it would WEAKEN bug 8b25's guard, whose whole purpose is refusing to write a parent Jira will not
    accept — and 8b25 was itself a defect fix. Loosening a guard to make a second guard reachable is how
    this epic got its 63-ticket incident.

### The empirical unknown, and how it gets settled

Whether `add_issues_to_epic` works against DC 8.17.1 under `agile_rest_path='greenhopper'` is NOT
established from documentation — the transport author called it a spike for that reason, and pycontribs
routes it to `POST /rest/greenhopper/1.0/epics/{epic_id}/add`, which some DC versions key by epic ID
rather than key. **This will be settled on the live harness, not by reading.** For anything with a live
oracle the harness is the arbiter — that is the lesson 2b16 and 88d9 both paid for. If the Agile call is
unavailable, the documented fallback is a direct write of the instance-discovered `Epic Link`
`customfield_NNNNN`; the fallback stays a fallback, and whichever path is used is recorded here with the
run id.

### AC4 — the silent-drop must end regardless of which path works

Independent of the Epic Link work: a parent that genuinely CANNOT be represented on the deployment must
raise an OPERATOR-VISIBLE signal instead of vanishing. Today `dispatch_one.py:571-578` swallows
`set_parent`'s exception (warn-and-continue), and on DC the emit gate drops the field before the decline
is even reached — which is why this class survived FIVE instances. This is the half of the ticket that
carries value even if the platform turns out to refuse the write, so it is built and tested
independently of the Epic Link path succeeding.

RED FIRST, per the standing direction on this epic: the pass-level overlap oracle is written and shown
RED before any transport change, so "no outbound parent was emitted for DC" is a failed ASSERTION rather
than a passing vacuous test.
